tabs.$description: Two visual styles per the user's own reference screenshots — segmented (a pill track, the active tab raised on a white pill) and underline (plain text, active tab marked by a blue bottom bar). Both share the same size grid and content variants (text-only, +icon-left, +counter, +icon+counter, icon-only). No hard cap on tab count is enforced by the component — that's a content decision, not a token; the tab list scrolls horizontally (overflow-x: auto) if it doesn't fit, and the docs page carries a practical (5-7 comfortable) guideline rather than a hard-coded number.

item.$description: Text stays 14px (size.base) at both sm and base — unlike button/input where type scales with the control size, here only icon size / padding / counter size scale; the label size is flat, per spec.

label.$description: Base (inactive) weight. Active state overrides fontWeight to weight.semibold only — same size/family/leading, see state.*.active.fontWeight in each style below.

counter.$description: Reuses component.counter.onNeutral exactly as built for the secondary button — inactive tab pairs with onNeutral.inactive (quiet gray.300 bg, dark label), active tab pairs with onNeutral.active (inverts to fill.primary blue, white label). Repurposes the same visual distinction (quiet vs. pops-blue) for tab-selection state instead of notification-freshness state — the tokens don't encode 'why', only how it looks, so this reuse is legitimate rather than a semantic stretch. No new counter tokens needed; sized via component.counter.size (sm/base, same keys).

segmented.$description: A recessed track — surface-0 (surface.page) fill + a surface-6 (outline.strong) hairline border, the same recessed pairing input/select use — holding the tabs; the active tab sits on it as a bg.active-tinted pill with an outline.active border. pillRadius (8px) = trackRadius (12px) − trackPadding (4px) — concentric corners, not a coincidence: an inset shape needs a proportionally smaller radius to look correctly nested inside its parent's rounded corner. trackPadding doubles as the gap between adjacent pills — tight by design, they're meant to read as one contained control, unlike underline's own (looser) inter-tab gap.

hover.$description: A 12% lighten layer over the surface-0 track — the sportsbook hover overlay (matching Search/Button). The tab is transparent at rest, so lighten.2 composites over the track rather than swapping to a baked colour.

underline.$description: No background at rest, plain text — the active tab is marked only by a 2px bottom bar (a literal in the generated CSS, not itself a scale value worth tokenizing — one visual step bolder than the 1px baseline it overlaps). A 1px baseline (border.default) spans the full tab list; the active indicator sits directly over it. Hover gets a 12% lighten pill (lighten.2), but as a fully-rounded rectangle inset 4px top/bottom so it floats clear of the baseline rather than running down to it — text-color-only hover was too subtle; a light rounded pill on hover while keeping the colored bar exclusive to the active tab is the common pattern (GitHub, Notion, Linear all do this).

inset.$description: 4px top/bottom inset for the hover pill, so it's a fully-rounded rectangle floating clear of the baseline (a 40px tab → ~32px pill, 32px → ~24px), not a bg running down to the line.
